entries.title: About Sebastien Rousseau | Frontmatter Gen Author
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Engineering & Pedigree About Sebastien Rousseau Principal systems architect building high-assurance Rust libraries, static site compilers, and deterministic document tooling. Sebastien Rousseau Principal Systems Architect · Creator of Frontmatter Gen, Noyalib & SSG Sebastien Rousseau has spent nearly two decades architecting, building, and securing high-throughput document processing engines, institutional financial systems, and open-source Rust libraries in London. Explore his publications, open-source portfolio, and advisory work at sebastienrousseau.com. Engineering Pedigree & Ecosystem Frontmatter Gen is part of a cohesive ecosystem of pure-Rust libraries engineered for static site compilation, structured metadata extraction, and standards-compliant parsing: Frontmatter Gen (frontmatter-gen): Zero-copy frontmatter extraction and multi-format parsing for YAML 1.2, TOML 1.1, and JSON with HTML meta tag synthesis and 100% unit test coverage. Noyalib (noyalib): Pure-Rust YAML 1.2 parser and serializer with zero unsafe code, configurable DoS budgets, and explicit YAML tag preservation. Static Site Generator (ssg / staticdatagen): Rust static site compiler with built-in WCAG AAA contrast auditing, Subresource Integrity (SRI), and CycloneDX SBOM generation. Skeletonic CSS: Accessible, token-driven CSS design system engineered for WCAG 2.2 Level AAA compliance across light and dark modes. Personal Website & Research: Visit sebastienrousseau.com for technical articles, architecture notes, and open-source releases.

entries.title: Accessibility Statement: WCAG 2.2 Level AAA Compliance
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Inclusive Engineering Accessibility Statement Dedicated to achieving WCAG 2.2 Level AAA compliance across all technical documentation and interactive components. Frontmatter Gen is committed to digital accessibility, conforming strictly to WCAG 2.2 Level AAA guidelines: Contrast Ratios: All 62 foreground/background token pairs across Light Mode and Dark Mode are mathematically verified by audit/contrast.py and scripts/audit-contrast.py to exceed the 7.0:1 AAA threshold for normal text (16.26:1 primary ink in Light Mode, 17.17:1 in Dark Mode). Keyboard Navigation: Full keyboard operability with visible focus rings, skip-to-content links, and Cmd/Ctrl + K search shortcuts. Screen Reader Support: Semantic HTML5 landmarks (header, nav, main, article, footer) and ARIA live regions across search and FAQ filters.

entries.title: API & CLI Reference: Rust Types, Functions & fmg Commands
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Developer Reference Rust API & CLI Reference Public types, zero-copy extractor functions, budget-guarded parsers, HTML meta tag synthesis, and CLI flags. Frontmatter Gen exposes a compact, strongly-typed Rust API alongside the fmg command-line binary. Every public function returns explicit Result types (ParseError, MetaError, ConfigError, EngineError) with zero panics on malformed user input. Full generated rustdoc is hosted on docs.rs/frontmatter-gen. 01 Core Library Interface & Value Model Extract and inspect frontmatter values using the unified Frontmatter map and recursive Value enum across YAML 1.2, TOML 1.1, and JSON: rust — frontmatter_gen::extract & Value use frontmatter_gen::{extract, Format, Frontmatter, Value}; use frontmatter_gen::parser::to_string; # Extract Frontmatter map and borrowed Markdown body let (fm, body): (Frontmatter, &str) = extract(content)?; # Inspect typed scalars, arrays, objects, or YAML 1.2 tags let title: Option<&str> = fm.get("title").and_then(Value::as_str); let draft: Option<bool> = fm.get("draft").and_then(Value::as_bool); let tagged = fm.get("custom").and_then(Value::as_tagged); # Serialize Frontmatter into YAML, TOML, or JSON let json_out: String = to_string(&fm, Format::Json)?; Core types and helper methods exported at the crate root: Type / Method Signature Description extract fn(&str) -> Result<(Frontmatter, &str), ParseError> Extracts and parses frontmatter in one pass, returning the parsed map and borrowed body slice. Frontmatter pub struct Frontmatter(pub HashMap<String, Value>) Case-sensitive map implementing Deref and DerefMut to HashMap<String, Value>. Value Null | Bool | Number | String | Array | Object | Tagged Format-agnostic recursive value enum with Value::Tagged(String, Box<Value>) for YAML 1.2 tags. Value::as_str / as_bool fn(&self) -> Option<...> Borrows the underlying string, boolean, f64, i64, u64, array, object, or tagged pair. Format Yaml | Toml | Json | Unsupported Identifies the detected or target serialization format for frontmatter blocks. 02 Zero-Copy Extractor & Budgeted Parser Modules The extractor, parser, and meta modules give fine-grained control over zero-copy slicing, structural DoS budgets, and HTML meta tag generation: Module Function Signature Purpose & Description extractor::extract_raw_frontmatter fn(&str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> Zero-copy split returning (raw_frontmatter, body) borrowed directly from content. extractor::detect_format fn(&str) -> Format Classifies raw frontmatter as Format::Json, Format::Toml, Format::Yaml, or Format::Unsupported. parser::parse fn(&str, Format) -> Result<Frontmatter, ParseError> Parses a raw frontmatter slice using default ParseOptions. parser::parse_with_options fn(&str, Format, &ParseOptions) -> Result<Frontmatter, ParseError> Parses raw frontmatter while enforcing validate, max_depth, and max_keys limits. parser::to_string fn(&Frontmatter, Format) -> Result<String, ParseError> Serializes a Frontmatter map into YAML, TOML, or pretty-printed JSON. meta::generate_metatags fn(&Frontmatter) -> MetaResult<String> Synthesizes entity-escaped HTML <meta>, Open Graph (og:*), and Twitter Card tags. 03 Command-Line Interface (fmg) & Error Diagnostics Compile with --features cli to use the fmg binary for extracting metadata or building static sites: bash — fmg subcommands # Extract frontmatter from an input file in JSON, YAML, or TOML format $fmg extract <INPUT> [--format json|yaml|toml] [--output <FILE>] # Build a static site from Markdown content and Tera templates (requires --features cli,ssg) $fmg build --content-dir <DIR> --output-dir <DIR> [--template-dir <DIR>] [--base-url <URL>] Structured error types returned across the crate: Error Type Module Description error::Error frontmatter_gen::error Crate-wide error enum covering extraction, parsing (`yaml_line`, `toml_line`), and I/O errors. error::ParseError frontmatter_gen::error Returned by extract, extractor, and parser for missing fences, format errors, or budget violations. meta::MetaError frontmatter_gen::meta Returned when a frontmatter key or value fails HTML meta tag validation. config::ConfigError frontmatter_gen::config Returned when ConfigBuilder validation fails (empty site name or invalid directory paths). 04 Stability & SemVer Contract In addition to Rust type and function signature stability, any change to the observable output of extract_metadata or generate_metatags for existing inputs is treated as a breaking change. Predictable API contract: zero-copy borrowing, budget-guarded parsing, and deterministic HTML meta tag emission.

entries.title: Pipeline Architecture: Zero-Copy Slicing & Parsing in Rust
entries.content:
Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Engine Internals Architecture & Pipeline Specifications How frontmatter-gen separates zero-copy slice extraction, format detection, DoS-guarded deserialization, and HTML meta tag synthesis. Frontmatter Gen is architected around a deterministic, four-stage pipeline that strictly decouples zero-copy boundary slicing from typed deserialization and downstream synthesis. Callers that only need to strip or inspect raw frontmatter pay zero heap allocation costs. Four-Stage Processing Pipeline 01 Boundary Slice Strip optional UTF-8 BOM (\u{FEFF}) and split (raw_frontmatter, body) as borrowed &str slices in a single forward scan. Zero Heap Allocations 02 Format Classifier Classify raw header slices as Format::Yaml, Format::Toml, Format::Json, or Format::Unsupported without regex overhead. O(n) Lexical Inspection 03 Guarded Parser Deserialize into Frontmatter via noyalib, toml, or serde_json while enforcing max_depth and max_keys budgets. Bounded Memory & Depth 04 Meta & SSG Emit Synthesize entity-escaped HTML <meta> tags, round-trip between formats via to_string, or render Tera templates. Deterministic Output Deterministic Pipeline Execution Trace The trace below illustrates how an input Markdown document flows through the four modules from raw &str slice to escaped HTML meta tags: pipeline-trace — frontmatter-gen v0.0.15 Input: &str ("---
title: Hello
country: NO
---
# Markdown Body") [Stage 1: extractor::extract_raw_frontmatter] Strip optional UTF-8 BOM • Locate closing --- fence [Stage 1: zero-copy output] raw = "title: Hello
country: NO" | body = "
# Markdown Body" (0 heap allocs) [Stage 2: extractor::detect_format] Heuristic scan -> Format::Yaml [Stage 3: parser::parse_with_options] noyalib YAML 1.2 parse • Check max_depth & max_keys invariants [Stage 4: meta::generate_metatags] Emit escaped <meta name="title"> and <meta name="country" content="NO"> Status: OK • Extractor Latency: ~120 ns • Unsafe Blocks: 0 Stage 1: Zero-Copy Boundary Slicing (src/extractor.rs) extractor::extract_raw_frontmatter(content: &str) -> Result<(&str, &str), ParseError> operates directly on the caller's UTF-8 string slice: UTF-8 BOM Handling: Automatically strips a leading \u{FEFF} byte-order mark before inspecting opening delimiters. Fence Scanning: Recognizes --- (YAML) and +++ (TOML) across both LF (
) and CRLF (
) line endings. Balanced JSON Braces: Tracks nesting depth for leading { ... } blocks while ignoring braces inside string literals and escape sequences. Stage 2 & 3: Format Detection & Budgeted Parsing (src/parser.rs) Once extracted, detect_format routes the raw slice to one of three pure-Rust parsers while ParseOptions enforces structural invariants: YAML 1.2 Engine (noyalib): Preserves explicit YAML tags as Value::Tagged(tag, Box<Value>) and avoids YAML 1.1 boolean coercion. TOML 1.1 Engine (toml): Converts TOML tables and native ISO 8601 datetimes into canonical Frontmatter entries. JSON Engine (serde_json): Parses RFC 8259 JSON objects with exact integer and floating-point preservation. DoS Budget Checks: check_depth and count_keys validate nesting depth and total key counts against ParseOptions. Modular compilation: zero-copy slicing, YAML 1.2 / TOML 1.1 / JSON parsing, and opt-in CLI and SSG feature flags. Stage 4: Meta Synthesis & Feature Isolation To keep compile times and dependency trees minimal for library consumers, heavy application dependencies are gated behind Cargo features: Feature Flag Default Included Modules & Dependencies default = [] Yes Core library (extractor, parser, meta, error, noyalib, toml, serde_json). cli Opt-in Adds the fmg binary target, clap CLI parser, tokio async runtime, and structured logging. ssg Opt-in Adds config, engine, fs, markdown, and template modules (tera + comrak).

entries.title: Performance Benchmarks: Criterion Suites & Zero-Copy Latency
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Performance Metrics Performance Benchmarks & Throughput Six dedicated Criterion benchmark suites measuring zero-copy slice extraction, multi-format parsing, and HTML meta tag synthesis. Frontmatter Gen ships with six reproducible Criterion.rs benchmark suites under benches/ covering every stage of the pipeline from zero-copy fence splitting to full static site page rendering. 0 B Extractor Heap Copy 6 Suites Criterion Benchmarks O(n) Single-Pass Scanner 01 Criterion Benchmark Suites (`benches/`) Each subsystem has a dedicated Criterion harness so performance regressions are isolated to the exact pipeline stage: Benchmark Target Source File Measured Operations extractor_bench benches/extractor_bench.rs Zero-copy extract_raw_frontmatter and detect_format across YAML, TOML, and JSON payloads. parser_bench benches/parser_bench.rs parser::parse, parse_with_options (with depth and key budgets), and to_string serialization. meta_bench benches/meta_bench.rs meta::generate_metatags over scalar, array, Open Graph, Twitter Card, and HTML-escaped fields. lib_bench benches/lib_bench.rs End-to-end frontmatter_gen::extract across small, medium, and large 1,000-key documents. config_bench benches/config_bench.rs ConfigBuilder construction, validation, and serialization under the ssg feature. error_bench benches/error_bench.rs Error and ParseError construction, line-number extraction, and Display formatting. 02 Reproducing Benchmarks Locally Run the Criterion suites on your own hardware to generate statistical HTML reports in target/criterion/: bash — cargo bench # Run all 6 Criterion benchmark suites $cargo bench --all-features # Run only the zero-copy extractor or parser benchmarks $cargo bench --bench extractor_bench $cargo bench --bench parser_bench 03 Allocation Profile by Pipeline Stage Because extractor::extract_raw_frontmatter only scans for opening and closing delimiters, its runtime is independent of the size of the Markdown body that follows the closing fence: Operation Time Complexity Heap Allocations extractor::extract_raw_frontmatter O(header_bytes) 0 allocations (borrows (&str, &str) from input) extractor::detect_format O(header_lines) 0 allocations (inspects trimmed slices in place) parser::parse_with_options O(header_bytes) 1 Frontmatter map + recursive Value nodes meta::generate_metatags O(keys) 1 output String buffer with entity-escaped tags Sub-microsecond slice extraction: Markdown bodies of any size are returned as zero-copy borrowed slices without scanning past the closing fence.

entries.title: Changelog & Release History: Frontmatter Gen
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Release History Changelog Every release increments strictly by +0.0.1 with signed tags, full test coverage, and zero unsafe code. All notable changes to Frontmatter Gen (frontmatter-gen) are documented below following strict +0.0.1 Semantic Versioning. [v0.0.15] - 2026-10-31 Fixed Resolved a Miri symbolic alignment check failure (_mm_load_si128 16-byte alignment requirement on 8-byte aligned slice inside memchr 2.8.2) during edge_case_tests::test_large_frontmatter by upgrading noyalib to 0.0.60. Added Reached 100.00% line, function, and region unit test coverage across all 10 source files (src/lib.rs, src/extractor.rs, src/parser.rs, src/meta.rs, src/error.rs, src/config.rs, src/engine.rs, src/fs.rs, src/markdown.rs, src/template.rs). [v0.0.14] - 2026-04-19 Changed Migrated YAML parsing and serialization from serde_yml (archived YAML 1.1) to pure-Rust noyalib (YAML 1.2) as recorded in ADR-0003. Preserved explicit YAML 1.2 tags via Value::Tagged(String, Box<Value>) and Value::as_tagged(). Added ParseOptions (validate, max_depth, max_keys) and parser::parse_with_options for configurable DoS budget enforcement. Added Miri verification with -Zmiri-strict-provenance -Zmiri-tree-borrows -Zmiri-symbolic-alignment-check, 4 cargo-fuzz targets, and cargo-vet supply-chain auditing. [v0.0.1 - v0.0.13] - 2023-2026 Added Core zero-copy frontmatter extraction (extractor::extract_raw_frontmatter), automatic format detection (detect_format), multi-format parsing (YAML, TOML, JSON), HTML meta tag synthesis (meta::generate_metatags), optional cli (fmg) binary, and optional ssg static site builder. Full historical release notes are available in the GitHub CHANGELOG.md.

Verified by verify-release-versions.sh Conventional Commits Imperative subject line (max 50 chars) with SSH/GPG signature (-S). entries.title: Supported Formats: YAML 1.2, TOML 1.1 & JSON Frontmatter
entries.content:
Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Specifications Matrix Supported Frontmatter Formats & Specifications Full YAML 1.2, TOML 1.1, and JSON frontmatter extraction, automatic format detection, and lossless cross-format conversion. Frontmatter Gen supports the three primary frontmatter formats used across static site generators, documentation engines, and content management systems. All three formats deserialize into the same Frontmatter (HashMap<String, Value>) representation and can be converted into one another via frontmatter_gen::parser::to_string. Format Fence / Delimiter Underlying Parser Specification & Key Guarantees YAML 1.2 --- ... --- noyalib (Pure Rust) YAML 1.2 Core Schema; no Norway problem; explicit tags preserved as Value::Tagged. TOML 1.1 +++ ... +++ toml TOML 1.1 tables, inline tables, arrays of tables, and ISO 8601 datetimes converted to strings. JSON { ... } or fenced JSON serde_json RFC 8259 balanced brace tracking with string-literal and escape-sequence awareness. 1. YAML 1.2 Frontmatter (---) via noyalib YAML is the default frontmatter format across Jekyll, Astro, Docusaurus, Eleventy, and Markdown documentation portals. Unlike legacy Rust crates built on archived serde_yaml (YAML 1.1), frontmatter-gen uses noyalib, a pure-Rust YAML 1.2 parser with zero unsafe code: No YAML 1.1 Norway Problem: In YAML 1.1, unquoted strings like NO, no, on, and off silently coerce into booleans. Under YAML 1.2, only true and false resolve as booleans, keeping country codes and short tokens intact as Value::String. Explicit YAML Tag Preservation: Tagged scalars and mappings (such as !custom value or !include path.yaml) are preserved losslessly as Value::Tagged(tag_name, Box<Value>) and accessible via Value::as_tagged(). Root Mapping Requirement: The top-level YAML value must be a mapping; scalar or sequence roots return ParseError::InvalidYaml. markdown — YAML 1.2 frontmatter --- title: "Deterministic YAML 1.2" country: NO published: true custom: !slug my-article-slug --- # Article Body 2. TOML 1.1 Frontmatter (+++) via toml TOML frontmatter is standard in Hugo, Zola, and Rust documentation pipelines. A TOML header opens with +++ on the first line and closes with a matching +++ fence: Native Datetime Normalization: TOML native datetimes (toml::Value::Datetime) are automatically converted into their canonical ISO 8601 string representation (Value::String) for uniform downstream template rendering. Nested Tables & Arrays: Dotted keys, inline tables, and nested sections map directly to nested Value::Object(Box<Frontmatter>) structures. markdown — TOML 1.1 frontmatter +++ title = "TOML 1.1 Frontmatter" weight = 10 date = 2026-10-31T12:00:00Z [taxonomies] categories = ["systems", "rust"] +++ # TOML Document Body 3. JSON Frontmatter ({ ... }) via serde_json JSON frontmatter is widely used in automated CMS exports and machine-generated Markdown documents. frontmatter-gen supports both standalone leading JSON objects and fenced JSON blocks: Balanced Brace Scanner: extract_json_frontmatter tracks brace depth while respecting quoted string literals and backslash escapes ("), ensuring braces inside string values never prematurely terminate extraction. Exact Numeric Representation: Numbers are stored as serde_json::Number inside Value::Number, preserving 64-bit signed/unsigned integers and IEEE 754 floats. 4. Cross-Format Serialization (parser::to_string) Because all three formats deserialize into Frontmatter, converting between YAML, TOML, and JSON requires a single call to frontmatter_gen::parser::to_string(&fm, target_format): rust — cross-format conversion use frontmatter_gen::{extract, Format}; use frontmatter_gen::parser::to_string; let (fm, _body) = extract("---
title: Convert Me
count: 42
---
Body")?; let as_toml = to_string(&fm, Format::Toml)?; let as_json = to_string(&fm, Format::Json)?;

entries.title: Getting Started: Install Frontmatter Gen Crate & CLI
entries.content:
Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Installation & Guide Getting Started with Frontmatter Gen Install the library crate or standalone CLI, extract YAML 1.2, TOML 1.1, and JSON headers, and synthesize HTML meta tags. Frontmatter Gen (frontmatter-gen) is an open-source, pure-Rust library and CLI for extracting and parsing YAML 1.2, TOML 1.1, and JSON frontmatter from Markdown and text documents. Follow this guide to add the crate, run the fmg binary, or enforce DoS limits on untrusted inputs. Core Library Crate v0.0.15 Zero-copy extractor, YAML 1.2 / TOML 1.1 / JSON parsers, and HTML meta tag generator with minimal dependencies. cargo add frontmatter-gen Standalone CLI Binary (fmg) Install the standalone fmg command-line binary with clap and tokio for terminal and CI workflows. cargo install frontmatter-gen --features cli SSG Engine Feature Flag Enable the static site generation engine powered by tera templates and comrak Markdown rendering. cargo add frontmatter-gen --features ssg Rust Toolchain MSRV 1.85.0+ Requires Rust 1.85.0 or newer (Edition 2024) and compiles cleanly across Linux, macOS, and Windows with zero unsafe code. rustup update stable 01 Extract & Parse Frontmatter in One Call The top-level frontmatter_gen::extract function detects the frontmatter format automatically, parses the header into a Frontmatter map, and returns the remaining Markdown body as a borrowed &str slice: rust — src/main.rs use frontmatter_gen::{extract, Value}; fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { let doc = "---
title: Zero-Copy Rust
published: true
---
# Welcome
"; let (fm, body) = extract(doc)?; assert_eq!(fm.get("title"), Some(&Value::String("Zero-Copy Rust".into()))); assert_eq!(fm.get("published"), Some(&Value::Bool(true))); assert!(body.starts_with("# Welcome")); Ok(()) } 02 Zero-Copy Raw Slicing & DoS Budget Guardrails When processing untrusted Markdown uploads or inspecting raw slices before allocation, pair extractor::extract_raw_frontmatter with parser::parse_with_options: rust — zero-copy & ParseOptions use frontmatter_gen::extractor::{detect_format, extract_raw_frontmatter}; use frontmatter_gen::parser::{parse_with_options, ParseOptions}; # 1. Borrow (raw_header, body) without heap allocation let (raw_header, body) = extract_raw_frontmatter(input)?; let format = detect_format(raw_header); # 2. Enforce structural depth and key-count budgets let options = ParseOptions { validate: true, max_depth: Some(8), max_keys: Some(64), }; let fm = parse_with_options(raw_header, format, &options)?; 03 Generate Escaped HTML Meta Tags & Use the CLI Convert parsed frontmatter into HTML <meta>, Open Graph, and Twitter Card tags, or invoke the fmg binary directly from your shell: bash — fmg cli quickstart # Extract frontmatter from a Markdown file and print as formatted JSON $fmg extract content/post.md --format json # Write extracted frontmatter to a YAML file $fmg extract content/post.md --format yaml --output build/meta.yaml # Build a static site from content/ and templates/ into public/ $fmg build --content-dir content --template-dir templates --output-dir public 04 Memory-Safe Execution Guarantees Every extraction and parsing pass executes strictly in local memory with #![forbid(unsafe_code)], verified under Miri Tree Borrows and continuous fuzzing: Zero-copy architecture: frontmatter boundaries are sliced in a single forward scan and parsed into strongly-typed Rust values with zero unsafe code.

entries.title: Made with Static Site Generator (SSG) | Web Platform
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Static Architecture Made with Static Site Generator (SSG) Why Frontmatter Gen documentation is statically compiled in Rust for uncompromising security, WCAG AAA accessibility, and instant loading. This site is natively compiled using the high-performance Static Site Generator (SSG) written in Rust and styled with Skeletonic CSS. Source of Truth: Content authored in Markdown (_posts/*.md) with frontmatter headers and Tera/Handlebars templates (_layouts/*.html). Compilation Speed: Full site generation in under 0.5 seconds with zero runtime JavaScript framework dependencies. Security & Provenance: Strict Subresource Integrity (SRI), Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, CycloneDX SBOM (sbom.cdx.json), and llms.txt / llms-full.txt bundles.

entries.title: Privacy Policy: Zero-Telemetry Documentation
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Trust & Governance Privacy Policy Our foundational commitment: zero tracking, zero analytics, zero external network requests, and complete local processing. Last updated: 31 October 2026 Frontmatter Gen is built on a strict zero-telemetry, zero-cookie architecture: No External Data Transmission: The frontmatter-gen library and fmg CLI execute entirely in local memory on your infrastructure. No document content, frontmatter fields, or usage telemetry are ever collected or transmitted. No Tracking Cookies: This documentation website (https://frontmatter-gen.com/) does not use tracking cookies, analytics pixels, or third-party behavioral scripts. Only your chosen colour theme (light, dark, or system) is stored locally in localStorage. Data Protection Compliance: Fully compliant with GDPR, UK Data Protection Act 2018, and California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).

entries.title: Security & Verification: Miri Tree Borrows, Fuzzing & Budgets
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Formal & Empirical Assurance Security Architecture & Trust Guarantees Defense-in-depth verification combining #![forbid(unsafe_code)], Miri Tree Borrows, structure-aware fuzzing, and configurable DoS budgets. Frontmatter parsers frequently sit at the trust boundary of content management systems, documentation portals, and static site pipelines where Markdown files arrive from external contributors or untrusted repositories. Frontmatter Gen enforces five layers of verification to ensure untrusted inputs cannot trigger memory unsafety, resource exhaustion, or HTML injection. 0 Unsafe #![forbid(unsafe_code)] 100% Unit Test Coverage 4 Targets LibFuzzer Harnesses 01 Memory Safety & Miri Tree Borrows Verification Both src/lib.rs and src/main.rs declare #![forbid(unsafe_code)], and the YAML 1.2 dependency noyalib is likewise 100% safe Rust. Every pull request runs the test suite under Miri with strict provenance and Tree Borrows aliasing checks: bash — miri tree borrows verification # Run Miri across minimal and default feature sets with Tree Borrows $MIRIFLAGS="-Zmiri-strict-provenance -Zmiri-tree-borrows -Zmiri-symbolic-alignment-check" cargo +nightly miri test --lib --no-default-features --locked $MIRIFLAGS="-Zmiri-strict-provenance -Zmiri-tree-borrows -Zmiri-symbolic-alignment-check" cargo +nightly miri test --lib --locked 02 DoS Budget Guardrails & Fuzzing Harnesses Untrusted YAML, TOML, or JSON headers can attempt denial-of-service via deeply nested structures or thousands of keys. parser::parse_with_options enforces deterministic budgets before returning a Frontmatter value, backed by four structure-aware cargo-fuzz targets: Verification Control Target / API Security Guarantee Nesting Depth Budget ParseOptions::max_depth Rejects YAML, TOML, or JSON trees nested deeper than max_depth levels. Key Count Budget ParseOptions::max_keys Rejects frontmatter payloads containing more than max_keys total keys across all maps. HTML Entity Escaping meta::generate_metatags Escapes &, <, >, ", and ' in all generated <meta> attributes. LibFuzzer Harnesses fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs Continuous fuzzing across extract_frontmatter, parse_yaml, parse_toml, and parse_json. Supply-Chain Audits cargo-deny, cargo-vet, cargo-audit Verifies license policies, RustSec advisories, and third-party crate audits on every CI run. 03 Vulnerability Disclosure Policy (RFC 9116) If you discover a security vulnerability in frontmatter-gen, please report it privately via GitHub Security Advisories or email sebastien.rousseau@gmail.com. See our machine-readable /.well-known/security.txt for RFC 9116 disclosure metadata. Defense-in-depth assurance: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], Miri Tree Borrows, 100% unit test coverage, and REUSE 3.3 licensing compliance.
headings: Memory Safety & Miri Tree Borrows Verification

entries.title: Use Cases: Static Site Generators, CMS & CI Pipelines
entries.content: Skip to main content Frontmatter Gen Menu Change colour theme System Production Blueprints Enterprise Use Cases & Deployment Patterns How engineering teams embed frontmatter-gen across static site compilers, multi-tenant CMS backends, and CI documentation gates. Frontmatter Gen is designed as a composable building block for any Rust service or CLI workflow that processes Markdown or structured text documents. 3 Formats YAML 1.2, TOML & JSON 0 B Copy Raw Slice Extraction 100% Safe Rust Execution 01 Static Site Generators & Documentation Portals Static site compilers frequently ingest thousands of Markdown pages authored across different eras or migrated from Hugo (TOML +++), Jekyll/Astro (YAML ---), or headless CMS exports (JSON { ... }). frontmatter-gen normalizes all three into a single Frontmatter type and synthesizes escaped HTML <meta> tags: Pipeline Capability Legacy Regex / YAML 1.1 Stack Frontmatter Gen Engine Supported Header Formats Separate crates per format Unified YAML 1.2, TOML 1.1 & JSON in one crate YAML 1.1 Norway Problem Unquoted NO / off coerced to booleans Strict YAML 1.2 preserves unquoted strings via noyalib Body Slicing Overhead Allocates new String copies of Markdown body Zero-copy borrowed &str via extract_raw_frontmatter SEO Meta Tag Generation Manual string concatenation prone to unescaped quotes Built-in entity-escaped meta::generate_metatags rust — static site page compiler use frontmatter_gen::{extract, meta::generate_metatags}; pub fn compile_page(source: &str) -> Result<(String, &str), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { let (frontmatter, markdown_body) = extract(source)?; let head_meta_tags = generate_metatags(&frontmatter)?; Ok((head_meta_tags, markdown_body)) } 02 Multi-Tenant Content APIs & Untrusted Upload Guardrails When accepting user-authored Markdown files over HTTP or webhook integrations, ParseOptions bounds recursion depth and total key counts before application logic runs: rust — untrusted webhook ingestion use frontmatter_gen::extractor::{detect_format, extract_raw_frontmatter}; use frontmatter_gen::parser::{parse_with_options, ParseOptions}; let (raw, body) = extract_raw_frontmatter(untrusted_markdown)?; let budget = ParseOptions { validate: true, max_depth: Some(6), max_keys: Some(50) }; let verified_fm = parse_with_options(raw, detect_format(raw), &budget)?; 03 CI/CD Documentation Linters & Cross-Format Migration Use the standalone fmg CLI in GitHub Actions or pre-commit hooks to validate that every Markdown document in a repository contains well-formed frontmatter and convert legacy TOML headers into JSON or YAML: bash — ci frontmatter validation & conversion # Validate and convert a TOML-header Markdown file's frontmatter to JSON $fmg extract docs/guide.md --format json --output /tmp/guide-meta.json Unified document metadata: ingest YAML 1.2, TOML 1.1, and JSON frontmatter across library, CLI, and static site pipelines.
headings: Multi-Tenant Content APIs & Untrusted Upload Guardrails
